issues.title: Finite-sample covariance rate

failure_location.quote: Central limit theorems connect the mean-field theory to the empirical reality through bounds of the form $\mathbb{E}\|\hat\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\mathrm F} \;\propto\:N^{-1/2}$   for i.i.d. and certain non-i.i.d. settings \cite{kallenberg1997foundations,hall2014martingale, feller1971introduction, le2009large}.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: To formalize all these claims, we will carry out the analysis of this paper in the \emph{mean–field} setting.
$\Pp_2(\R^d)$ is the set of Borel probability measures on $\R^d$ with finite second moment.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that i.i.d. sampling connects the paper's mean-field theory to empirical covariances through an expected Frobenius error proportional to N^{-1/2}. The old paper actually assumes only finite second moments and provides no fourth-moment condition supporting this rate. For a centered symmetric scalar law with tail probability asymptotic to t^{-p}, where 2<p<3, the variance is finite. Nevertheless, a single outlier of size proportional to sqrt(N), with the remaining sample sum typical, has probability of order N^{1-p/2} and causes an order-one empirical-variance error. Consequently the expected error can decay at that slower order, not at O(N^{-1/2}). The claimed empirical rate therefore exceeds what the old paper's P2 scope supports.
issues.overall_effect: The generic root-N justification for passing from finite ensembles to population covariances fails for admissible heavy-tailed P2 distributions. The paper's population-level definitions, theorems, and proofs remain unaffected because they do not use a finite-sample covariance rate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rewrite the empirical-covariance sentence as a conditional bound: for i.i.d. draws with finite fourth moment, state that E||hatSigma−Sigma||_F <= C N^(-1/2), and make any non-i.i.d. extension conditional on explicit analogous moment and dependence assumptions. Also clarify that membership in P_2 alone supplies no universal root-N rate. The population-level results require no alteration.
issues.why_classification: The repair is local, but the old P_2 scope and the asserted root-N rate cannot both be retained. Preserving the rate requires excluding the natural and substantial class of finite-variance, infinite-fourth-moment laws; retaining all of P_2 requires surrendering the universal rate. This is a limited weakening of an isolated prose claim, with no affected formal results or global reconstruction, so it is moderate rather than minor or serious.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: given sufficient regularity, the variance is $\mathcal O(N^{-\alpha})$

issues.title: ETKF anomaly-transform normalization

failure_location.quote: \hat T \hat T ^\top  =  I_N - \left(\hat X_f^{(c)}\right)^\top H^\top\left(H\hat C_fH^\top + \Gamma\right)^{-1}H\hat X_f^{(c)}.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \hat C_a := \frac{1}{N-1}\hat X_a \left(I_N - \frac{1}{N}\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^\top\right)\hat X_a^\top,\quad  C_a = \hat C_f - \hat C_fH^\top (H\hat C_fH^\top + \Gamma)^{-1}H\hat C_f.

issues.failure_explanation: Writing the centered forecast matrix as Xc gives Cf=(N-1)^{-1}XcXc^T. The analysis anomalies produced by the principal transform have covariance (N-1)^{-1}Xc(TT^T)Xc^T. With the old TT^T, this equals Cf-(N-1)Cf H^T(HCfH^T+Gamma)^{-1}H Cf, rather than the required Cf-Cf H^T(HCfH^T+Gamma)^{-1}H Cf. Thus the decrement is too large by N-1; for admissible ensembles with N>2 the old square-root argument can also become indefinite.
issues.overall_effect: The stated linear-model ETKF construction need not satisfy its advertised Gaussian-consistent covariance condition and may not define the stipulated principal symmetric square root. The main EnKU formal results and the separately specified EAKF updates do not depend on this erroneous normalization.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace both the ETKF second-moment equation and its repeated principal-square-root formula by TT^T = I_N − (N−1)^(-1)(X_f^(c))^T H^T(H C_f H^T + Gamma)^(-1)H X_f^(c), and define T using the principal square root of this corrected right-hand side. The remaining ETKF discussion and the separate EnKU and EAKF constructions can remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: A one-line covariance calculation using C_f=(N−1)^(-1)X_f^(c)(X_f^(c))^T uniquely identifies the missing normalization and restores the advertised analysis covariance and positive-semidefinite square-root argument. The defect is substantive rather than purely typographical because the literal algorithm can be undefined or produce the wrong covariance, but its complete repair is short, routine, local, and preserves every intended guarantee without affecting dependent results.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: \hat T \hat T ^\top  =  I_N -\frac{1}{N-1} \left(\hat X_f^{(c)}\right)^\top H^\top\left(H\hat C_fH^\top + \Gamma\right)^{-1}H\hat X_f^{(c)}.
